issues.description: validate_conda checks for substring 'mamba' which also matches 'micromamba' and risks false positives
issues.detail: The substring search `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ['micromamba', 'mamba', 'conda'])` is loose: any executable whose --version output happens to contain the word 'conda' (e.g., a wrapper script mentioning 'anaconda') would pass. A stricter invariant would parse the leading token of the version string (e.g., split first whitespace) and compare against a known set. State the invariant: 'output begins with one of {conda, mamba, micromamba} followed by a version string'.

issues.description: validate_conda silently returns True for empty string, conflating 'unset' with 'valid'
issues.detail: The early `if conda_executable == '': return True` overloads the function: callers cannot distinguish 'no path provided' from 'path is a valid conda'. This is the kind of ambiguity that creates downstream off-by-one logic. Either return a tri-state (None for unset) or document the invariant explicitly in the docstring: 'empty string is treated as no-op valid because the form is unfilled'. The reader should not have to infer this.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' on the file browser will hide valid conda binaries on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: The conda/mamba/micromamba executables on POSIX systems have no `.exe` suffix. A user on Linux opening the browser dialog will see no candidates and have to bypass the filter. The data-structure choice here (single filter string) is paying interest: the right structure is platform-aware filters, e.g., `'*.exe' if sys.platform == 'win32' else '*'`.

issues.description: The function name validate_conda overstates its guarantee; rename or document
issues.detail: The function validates 'a path that looks like it could be a conda-family executable by name in --version output.' That is weaker than 'this is a working conda.' A literate-programming-grade comment would state the precise predicate. Consider renaming to `looks_like_conda_executable` or stating the invariant explicitly in the docstring: 'returns True iff the file is executable AND --version output names one of {conda, mamba, micromamba}; returns True for empty string as a sentinel for unset.'

issues.description: run_program subprocess in validate_conda has no timeout; user-supplied path could hang the UI thread
issues.detail: `run_program(conda_executable, ['--version']).communicate()` will block indefinitely if the user points at a hung or interactive binary (e.g., a shell that reads stdin). The validation runs in the preferences dialog, which is on the UI thread. Add a `communicate(timeout=...)` and handle TimeoutExpired by killing the process and returning False. Termination of the validation routine is currently not obvious from the code.

issues.description: out.decode() assumes default encoding; could raise UnicodeDecodeError on non-UTF-8 systems
issues.detail: When users have unusual locale settings (Windows CP-1251, etc.) and a hostile binary returns non-UTF-8 bytes, `.decode()` without arguments uses utf-8 strict and will raise. The except clause swallows it, so the function returns False — but the failure mode is silent. Prefer `out.decode(errors='replace')` and document why.

issues.description: Local variable `valid` is set but the early-return in except makes the structure unnecessarily branchy
issues.detail: The function mixes early-returns (file not found, not executable, exception) with a flag-and-fall-through pattern at the end. For a reader: the invariant 'valid is False unless --version names a known tool' is harder to verify than necessary. A cleaner literate form would early-return True/False at each gate and end with `return False`. Small, but this is exactly the kind of code where the reader-as-constraint matters.

issues.description: create_browsefile now takes validate_callback/validate_reason but the contract of validate_callback is undocumented
issues.detail: The new keyword arguments are forwarded to create_lineedit with no docstring update on create_browsefile itself. A reader of the public surface must follow two hops to learn that validate_callback receives the file path and must return truthy on valid. Add a one-paragraph docstring stating the callable's signature, when it is invoked, and what truthy/falsy mean for the UI.

issues.description: edit.setFocus() side effect in select_file changes prior behavior with no comment explaining why
issues.detail: The unrelated `edit.setFocus()` call after `edit.setText(filename)` will trigger focus-out validation on whatever widget previously had focus. This may be intentional (to fire the new validate_callback on the newly populated path), but the diff offers no explanation. A literate comment should state: 'setFocus is required so that the validate_callback added in this PR fires after the browse dialog populates the field.'

review.summary: The change is small and mostly mechanical: add a config key, a UI group, and a validator. Algorithmically there is little to audit — no loops, no non-trivial data structures — so the rigor focus falls on the predicate `validate_conda` and the contracts around it. The validator's invariant ('this path is a usable conda-family executable') is weaker than its name suggests: substring matching on --version output, no subprocess timeout, decode assumptions, and conflation of empty-string-as-unset with valid-as-checked all leave the predicate under-specified. The Windows-only `*.exe` filter is the kind of data-structure choice (single string vs platform-aware) that will pay interest on Linux/macOS. UNDER-AUDITED overall; not WRONG, just under-stated for code that lives on the boundary between user input and subprocess execution.
